w10_T4_003432: A cycling club had 148 water bottles in its store, and a sponsor sent 68 more. The whole stock was then split into 2 equal shares, one for the road team and one for the track team. The road team's coach Bella collected her team's share. A shop later donated 32 bottles to the road team, and the track coach Marc passed over 31 that his own team no longer needed, which left Marc with fewer bottles than Bella. The club records its ride times in minutes even though the newsletter prints them in hours. How many bottles did the road team have?
w10_T4_003433: On Monday morning a garden centre potted 132 seedlings on each of its 3 benches. Before lunch a volunteer added 10 more seedlings to the batch. In the afternoon the manager Ines had every seedling divided into 4 plugs for growing on. Her colleague Rafa handled fewer plugs that day than Ines did. In the evening a delivery brought 48 more plugs, and Rafa found 15 in a spare tray. How many plugs did the garden centre have?
w10_T4_003434: A school music room started the term with 171 reeds for its clarinets. 93 reeds were handed out to beginners, and 75 more split and were thrown away. Each reed still in the box was packaged with 6 spare ligatures for a fundraising sale. The music room has 24 music stands. 11 of the ligatures were lost in transit, and a supplier then sent 69 more. The teacher logs practice in minutes even though the reports to parents are given in hours. How many ligatures did the music room have?
w10_T4_003450: A stationery supplier had 114 boxes of pens in the depot and doubled that stock with a second delivery of the same size. A damp store room ruined 47 of the boxes. Every box that was still good holds 9 pens. Each pen is sold with 2 spare refills, and the supplier counted the refills it would need. The identical order was then placed for each of 7 regional depots. How many refills did the supplier need in total?
w10_T4_003453: A hostel kitchen began the week with 93 jars of jam. 5 jars were broken when a shelf gave way. A donation added 59 jars. Guests ate their way through 55 jars, and a school trip took another 73 away. A dozen of the jars are the marmalade kind kept for staff, and the kitchen has 8 fridges along the back wall. 4 more jars went mouldy, and a supplier then delivered 56 fresh ones. How many jars of jam did the kitchen have?
w10_T4_003461: A youth theatre had 14 costumes in store and borrowed 78 more from a neighbouring group, a dozen of them Victorian. Each costume needs 5 minutes of pressing before a show. The pressing work was shared equally among the 4 wardrobe helpers, and Dita took one of those shares of the minutes. She then spent 19 more minutes repairing a hem. The company writes these totals in minutes even though the production budget is set out in hours. Dita repeated exactly that amount of work before each of the 4 performances, and she spent a further 62 minutes on repairs on the closing night. How many minutes of work did Dita do in all?
w10_T4_003463: A hardware shop had 114 tins of varnish and sold 77 of them in a spring sale. A wholesaler then delivered 56 more tins. A dozen of the tins are the clear matt finish. Every tin covers 9 square metres of decking. One customer's decking measures 200 square metres. An opened tin added 6 square metres of coverage to the shop's total, and a returned tin added 47 more. How many square metres of decking could the shop's stock cover?
w10_T4_003466: A driving school had 163 lesson slots booked for the month. 86 slots were used in the first week and 27 in the second. Bad weather forced 47 slots to be cancelled altogether. A new instructor then added 59 slots to the diary. Every slot still in the diary needs 8 pages of paperwork. The office records lesson lengths in minutes even though the invoices to learners quote hours. How many pages of paperwork does the diary require?
w10_T4_003470: A ferry company sold 240 tickets on each of its 6 morning sailings. Cancellations took 1355 tickets out of that total, and a coach party then bought 23. Each remaining ticket entitles the holder to 6 luggage tags, and the company counted the tags it would need. Every tag is printed in 4 copies, one for each desk. The company records crossing times in minutes although the timetable is published in hours. A printer added 8 spare copies to the batch. How many printed copies were there?
w10_T4_003471: A cafe had 177 loyalty cards in circulation and issued 68 more in one week. 55 cards were filled up and handed back, and 3 were reported lost. Every card still in circulation carries 4 unused stamp spaces, and the manager Odette counted those spaces. Her colleague Ravi counted fewer spaces on his own set of cards than Odette did. Odette then crossed out 29 spaces that had expired. The cafe records its opening times in minutes even though the door sign gives them in hours. How many stamp spaces did Odette's count come to?
w10_T4_003475: A scout group brought 17 tents to camp, and each tent sleeps 5 people. 55 of the sleeping places were taken by leaders and were not offered to the children. Every place still free was worth 5 meal tickets at the camp kitchen. The kitchen then issued 72 extra meal tickets for visitors. Over the weekend 175 meal tickets were handed in at the servery. The camp records its cooking times in minutes even though the rota is written in hours. How many meal tickets were still unused?
w10_T4_003480: Hugo bakes 27 shortbread rounds on each of the 5 trays he owns. A neighbour gave him 80 more rounds for the village sale. His sister Mia contributed 45, although Mia had baked fewer rounds than Hugo. The village hall has 96 chairs. Hugo then repeated his whole collection 5 times over, so that every stall at the fair could have the same amount. How many shortbread rounds did Hugo end up with?
w10_T4_003481: A repair shop had 132 bicycle inner tubes on the rack. 118 tubes went out with a bulk order, and 10 more were found perished. A delivery brought 28 tubes back into stock, and 9 were used on same-day repairs. A dozen of the tubes are the wide sort for mountain bikes. Each tube still on the rack is bagged with 8 patches for sale. The shop times its repairs in minutes although the quotes to customers are given in hours. How many patches does the shop need for that bagging?
w10_T4_003483: A printer produced 175 posters for each of the 7 towns in a campaign. A late order added 17 more posters. Half of all the posters went to the northern region and half to the southern region, and the campaign manager Ilse took charge of the northern half. Her colleague Gus looked after fewer posters than Ilse did. Ilse was then given 76 extra posters that Gus could not use. Every poster in her care was fixed to a wall with 8 pins. How many pins did Ilse need?
w10_T4_003484: Nia had 51 handmade candles ready for a market. She made 30 more on Saturday and was given 36 by her friend Otto, who had made fewer candles than Nia. She then tripled her whole stock by working through a long weekend. A wholesaler added 65 candles for her to sell on their behalf. Shoppers bought 266 candles during the market. How many candles did Nia have left?
w10_T4_003486: On Monday morning a depot had 235 pallets of bottled water. Later that morning a supplier delivered 77 more, and in the afternoon a returned order added 53. In the evening 69 pallets were sent out to a festival. Every pallet still in the depot carries 9 crates of bottles. The supervisor Nils counted more crates than his colleague Aina did on her own aisle. The depot logs its loading times in minutes even though the haulage contract is written in hours. How many crates were in the depot?
w10_T4_003488: A stadium sold 112 season tickets in the first week and 34 in the second. Each season ticket admits the holder to 4 matches. Every match ticket is printed with 5 detachable vouchers, and the club counted all of those vouchers. Supporters redeemed 2176 vouchers over the season. The club records its kick-off times in minutes rather than in hours. How many vouchers were left unredeemed?
w10_T4_003492: A charity had 230 blankets in its warehouse and received 13 more from a school. A shelter then took 49 blankets away. Every blanket that was left was packed with 4 tins of food, and the coordinator Petra counted the tins. Her colleague Marek counted fewer tins on his own shift than Petra did. Petra took 21 dented tins out of the count. A matching donor then doubled the number of tins the charity held. How many tins did the charity have?
w10_T4_003495: Sofia grows tomato plants in 2 identical polytunnels, and each polytunnel holds 111 plants. A neighbour gave her 13 more plants, and she raised 9 herself on the windowsill. Slugs destroyed 4 of the plants. She then shared the whole lot equally among the 6 members of the allotment society, and her friend Bram took one of those shares. Bram had grown fewer plants of his own than Sofia had. How many plants did Bram take?
w10_T4_003497: A community garden had 34 tools in its shed, a dozen of them long-handled, and bought 4 more. 11 tools were returned to the lender they had come from. A grant then paid for 49 new tools. 3 tools were broken during a work day, and 3 replacements arrived the next morning. Every tool in the shed needs 7 minutes of cleaning after use, and the garden adds those minutes up. The rota is written in minutes although the volunteers' agreement talks about hours. How many minutes of cleaning does one full round of the shed take?
w10_T4_003502: A youth club had 115 board games and was given 20 more by a library. 55 games were passed on to a hospital. The rest were shared equally among the 5 rooms of the club, and the games room took one of those shares. Those games were then divided equally between the 4 tables in that room, and Nour took charge of one table, having brought fewer games from home than her friend Sami had. Every game on Nour's table has 7 playing pieces. Nour found that 27 pieces were missing altogether. How many playing pieces were still on Nour's table?
w10_T4_003503: A cafe had 80 cupcakes and packed them equally into 4 display boxes, and Rosa took one box to her stall. Rosa sold 16 cupcakes from that box during the morning. She then cut every cupcake she had left into 2 halves to sell as tasters. Her colleague Diego sold fewer tasters that day than Rosa did. The tasters Rosa had not sold were shared equally between 2 staff rooms, and she carried one of those shares back to the cafe. 3 of the tasters in that share were dropped on the way. How many tasters did Rosa deliver to the cafe?
w10_T4_003505: On Monday morning a school hall had 69 chairs stacked at the back, and the caretaker brought in 72 more. Every chair carries 6 rubber feet, and the caretaker counted the feet before an inspection. Later that morning he found 5 spare feet in a drawer. The hall itself is 32 metres long. During the afternoon 511 worn feet were stripped off and thrown away. In the evening a delivery brought 5 replacement feet. How many rubber feet did the caretaker count at the end?
w10_T4_003506: On Saturday morning a florist had 60 buckets of cut flowers. 48 buckets were emptied for a wedding before noon. At lunchtime a grower delivered 33 more buckets. During the afternoon 23 buckets were sold to a hotel. The shop front is 7 metres wide. In the evening the florist made 9 bouquets from every bucket she still had, and a friend brought 35 finished bouquets to add to the display. How many bouquets were on the display?
w10_T4_003527: A library had 155 audio players to lend out. 96 of them were borrowed in the first week, and 57 more went out in the second. The library is open 6 days a week. 1 player came back broken and was scrapped. A donor named Elke then gave the library 22 players, which was more than her colleague Toma had ever donated. How many audio players did the library have available?
